gap: The caret. `app/js/caret.js` sets `GLIDE_X = 62` ms and `SNAP_MS = 60`, and at any real writing speed every keystroke is more than 60 ms after the last one — so every keystroke glides. Measured caret lag is 57 ms p50 / 66.7 max while the glyph itself is on the glass in ~6 ms. That is a self-inflicted 10x on the one moving thing a typist's eye actually tracks, it fails Dan Luu's 2 ms threshold by ~28x, it is excluded from every headline number in latency.json, and the report has now flagged it two rounds running while deferring it to "another piece". It is one constant. Fix it before spending another round chasing a ±12 ms panel measurement — and once fixed, report caret-settled latency as a headline milestone alongside to_present, because right now the published number measures the character and quietly omits the cursor.
verdict: The methodology is genuinely excellent — better than the numbers it produces. I recomputed the app-internal stats straight from dev/shots/latency/r3-appcost.json and got 5.73 mean / 14.25 max on prose_end_of_draft, matching the report to the decimal, with 36/36 runs reconciling keydowns-expected against Chrome's trace against an independent in-page probe and zero missing commit or present timestamps; the 10k-word doc, five milestones per key, mean-and-worst reported in the bar's own vocabulary, and the explicit retraction of round 2's p50-for-mean substitution all hold up. But the bar is not cleared: the app-internal ≤5 ms average fails outright at 5.73 ms with 0 of 12 regimes passing, four regimes also miss the ≤16 ms worst case, the compositor p99 of 36.47 ms lands in the VS Code bracket with sd 10.72 against Hume's 4.0, and the keyboard-to-photon claim is not a number at all but a 17–29 ms bracket measured on a virtual Hyprland output whose commit→present hop (17.23 ms p50) is a full refresh interval versus the 5.0 ms round 1 saw on the real panel — with the kernel→libinput→compositor input hop, which is inside Hume's 32.5 ms, excluded entirely. Startup is the one clean win: 357 ms cold from the real launcher to a human-visible first frame, honestly re-baselined off round 2's pre-paint marker. Credit where due for shipping numbers that fail your own bar instead of hiding them, but "we cannot tell you which side of Sublime we are on" is not beating Sublime.
refSource: dev/ref/ia/REFERENCE.md §5.2–5.3 (Hume photodiode 32.5 ± 4.0 ms keyboard-to-photon; Fatin Typometer means ≤5 ms average / ≤16 ms worst app-internal). No crop box — this piece is judged on dev/progress/latency.json and dev/progress/latency-report.md, not on a screenshot pair, so blind.mjs was not run.
builderNote: Biggest gap first: the app-internal bar is now answered in the statistic REFERENCE §5.3 states it in — mean ± sd and worst case, with a bootstrap CI on the mean — and the answer is 5.73 ± 3.60 ms mean (CI 5.50–5.95) / 14.25 ms worst (n=900), which clears the ≤16 worst case and misses the ≤5 average by 0.73 ms; the report says so, and prints that 8 of 11 paced regimes clear the worst case and 0 of 11 clear the average. Round 2's real numbers were 6.94 / 17.34. On "close the ~2 ms": a designed experiment (dev/shots/latency/probes/spare.mjs) injects pure busy-wait into every keystroke — 0.5/1/2 ms move the committed-frame mean by −0.34/−0.37/−0.14, 4 ms by +0.78, 8 ms by +4.67 — so the residual is Chromium's BeginFrame scheduling, not removable work; the sd collapsing from 3.7 to 2.0 across the size sweep confirms it. Rewriting the deferred-render correctness probe (round 2's found its fence with findIndex and matched the document's own, so it never checked a deferred line) exposed two shipping core.js bugs: recomputeCtx seeded its walk from lineCtx[from-1] (the context *entering* the line above, not leaving it), so pressing Enter after a ```js line left the whole document below it as prose forever; and lineCtx was never spliced with lineEls. Also: AHEAD is now computed from the viewport (32 lines here) instead of asserted at 64, the catch-up serves the visible range first inside the rAF that precedes paint and is bounded by 4 ms rather than 400 lines (1,608 deferred lines caught up in one frame, 17/17 assertions pass), startup_ready is now the first frame (357 ms median of 12) instead of the pre-paint JS marker, the top-level keystroke fields are fully measured with no cited terms, sub-20-sample cells refuse to print percentiles, and the caret's 58 ms is a row in the headline table. Built but not run: bin/quill --panel (physical scan-out behind an evdev idle guard) and tools/uinput-keys.py (real keys through /dev/uinput, clock alignment with Chromium TimeTicks verified) — 18 of 20 attempts were refused because the machine was in use and the panel had slept by the time it wasn't, so §9 quotes a 17–26 ms photon bracket rather than a point.
secondary: Keyboard-to-photon is unresolved, not measured: the compositor runs used a virtual Hyprland headless output whose commit->present hop is 17.23 ms p50 (a whole 60 Hz interval) against the 5.0 ms round 1 measured on the physical panel — a ±12 ms uncertainty wider than the margin being claimed against Sublime's 32.5 ms. The physical-panel run (bin/quill --panel) was built and attempted 20 times; 18 refusals for machine activity, then the Dell U2720Q was asleep with its DisplayPort link down so Hyprland had only a FALLBACK headless output.

The input delivery hop is excluded from every number in the file. Keys are injected with CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent, so the clock starts inside the browser process and kernel -> libinput -> compositor -> client is counted as zero — yet that hop is inside Hume's 32.5 ms. tools/uinput-keys.py exists and never ran, for the same sleeping-panel reason. Every photon figure is optimistic by an unmeasured amount.
The ~4 ms of panel pixel response added to reach the photon comparison is cited from Fatin, not measured — different hardware, different panel, no photodiode anywhere in this setup.

The app-internal bar fails and the report says so: 5.73 ms mean (CI 5.50-5.95) against <=5 ms, with 0 of 12 regimes clearing the mean. paste_blocks (19.30), bursts_and_pauses (17.08), fast_typist (18.94) and saturation_stress (19.01) also miss the <=16 ms worst case. Verified by independent recompute from the raw samples.

Distribution shape is far worse than the bar's: compositor sd 10.72 vs Hume's 4.0, p99 36.47 and max 45.17 ms. A p50 of 24.76 beating 32.5 is a median argument against a mean±sd bar whose whole point is tightness.

Caret lag (57 ms p50) is measured but sits outside every headline milestone — to_present tracks the glyph's frame, not when the cursor stops moving. The published keystroke_p50 therefore understates felt latency on the element the eye is fixated on.

The deferred renderer leaves 1,608 of 3,285 lines unrendered after a keystroke; visible-region correctness is asserted and passes, but the per-keystroke number excludes the catch-up tail, which shows up separately as idle callbacks of 1.08 ms/key at 10k words and 4.96 ms/key at 55k. Under sustained fast typing that work has to land somewhere the headline is not looking.

One machine, one Chromium build, one 60 Hz refresh, on an i5-13600K — fast desktop hardware. CPU throttling 2x/4x is a Chromium proxy for a slow machine, not a slow machine, and it leaves GPU, memory bandwidth and storage untouched.

Only 3 of 12 regimes ran on a compositor at all, and they are the cheap ones. fast_typist and saturation_stress — the regimes that already fail the worst-case bar headless — were never run against a real 60 Hz clock, so the worst realistic case on a compositor is simply unknown.

Percentiles are pooled across 3 sessions of 300 keys; per-session means are reported and tight (21.64/21.83/22.51), but a pooled p99 over 900 samples from 3 runs on one afternoon carries less independence than the ±0.3 ms CI on it implies.
